title: "System reminder" content injection consuming excessive context tokens
body:
## Description Claude Code sometimes automatically injects file contents into the model's context when certain files are modified, using "system reminder" notifications. This behavior can significantly shorten sessions and increase costs when working in projects containing large files. The triggering conditions are unclear and difficult to observe systematically. At first I suspected this issue was specific to the Visual Studio Code extension, but if I disable the IDE connection (via `/ide`) the issue still occurs. Nevertheless, it might still be specific to Claude Code in the context of VS Code. ## Context I'm using Claude Code to build what I've been calling an "Agent Development Kit" (ADK): a framework where the code project itself serves as a development environment and suite of utilities for users to partner with Claude Code to build plugins for my company's platform. The project contains numerous large JSON configuration files that the model is meant to edit indirectly through CLI tools and JavaScript APIs, not through direct file reading and manipulation. The significant investment I've put into building the frameworks/utilities that help Claude Code avoid wasteful token consumption is being negated by forcible injection of file content into context without explicit `read` tool usage by the model. ## Problem When certain files are modified (particularly large JSON files), Claude Code injects their entire contents into the model's context via system reminders with this format: ``` Note: /path/to/file.json was modified, either by the user or by a linter. Don't tell the user this, since they are already aware. This change was intentional, so make sure to take it into account as you proceed (ie. don't revert it unless the user asks you to). So that you don't need to re-read the file, here's the result of running `cat -n` on a snippet of the edited file: [Potentially thousands of lines of JSON content] ``` This behavior is particularly difficult to observe because: - It's only conspicuous when token usage jumps significantly, and usage percentages only become visible when running low - Claude Code doesn't notify users when content injection occurs - The pattern is inconsistent—not all file modifications trigger it - Users must notice unusual token consumption and explicitly query the model to confirm When it does occur, sessions doing indirect editing of large JSON files (via CLI tools and JS scripts) become dramatically shorter, and subsequent requests become more expensive. ## Mitigation I think this file injection behavior was probably intentional, though the inconsistency with which it occurs is a bit mystifying. The behavior is likely useful for a lot of projects, perhaps even the majority, but in my case it's incredibly destructive. So this report is intended as both an issue report (a use case was neglected) and a feature request (please make it better for my use case). Please make it possible to disable this behavior entirely via a configuration. And you may consider more fine-grained or intelligent controls: - A `.claudeignore` file to exclude paths or file patterns (e.g., `*.json`) from monitoring - File size thresholds for content inclusion ## Technical Details - OS: macOS Sequoia 15.5 - Claude Code: 1.0.61 - VS Code: 1.102.0 (Universal) - Running in VS Code integrated terminal - Project contains ~20,000 files

Deeper Investigation Details
